principles: Active user-facing and generated agent-role surfaces should use Lattice naming only.
Role ID migration must preserve reviewer/gate semantics rather than weakening evidence requirements.
Compatibility should be explicit and narrow: only historical/archive/runtime-compatibility references may keep Koala wording when renamed behavior would be misleading.
Verification must include both text inventory and executable CLI/build checks.
drivers: The user wants a clean Lattice surface with no active Koala legacy identity.
koala-* role IDs are embedded in templates, generated assets, dispatch, reviewer gates, and docs.
A broad string replacement could break signed evidence lanes or historical metadata interpretation.
Host assets changed, so Codex/Claude adapter verification is required.

options.name: A: Hard active rename with explicit historical boundary
pros: Removes active Koala role IDs from CLI/templates/runtime docs as requested.
Keeps a narrow allowance for archival or compatibility strings where removal would corrupt historical meaning.
Allows tests to assert the new Lattice surface without pretending old records never existed.
cons: Requires touching more files and updating tests/registry fixtures carefully.
Some legacy runtime environment variable names may remain until a separate compatibility story.

options.name: B: Template-only rename
pros: Smaller patch and lower immediate test surface.
Quickly removes the most visible koala-implementer template names.
cons: Runtime help, review lanes, process-fact registry, and generated assets would still emit Koala role IDs.
Does not satisfy the user request to clean all active Koala naming.

options.name: C: Global blind replacement of every Koala token
pros: Maximizes apparent cleanup in one pass.
cons: High risk of corrupting historical docs, legacy compatibility constants, env var contracts, and migration tests.
Would make it harder to distinguish active product identity from old archive material.

chosen: A: Hard active rename with explicit historical boundary
rationale: Choose A because the user wants active Koala naming removed, but process facts and archival material need a controlled boundary. The migration should change canonical role IDs to lattice-* while preserving or clearly labeling unavoidable historical/runtime-compatibility references.

preMortem.scenario: Reviewer gate stops accepting review evidence after role IDs change.
preMortem.trigger: review_run_start or finding_add still checks koala-review-* prefix while templates use lattice-review-*.
preMortem.consequence: Stories cannot progress through REVIEW or TEST.
preMortem.mitigation: Update review-run lane lists, prefix checks, process-fact registry, guard text, tests, and run targeted story/review smoke tests.

preMortem.scenario: Generated host assets drift from canonical templates.
preMortem.trigger: Only packages/main/templates are renamed, while .claude/.Codex mirrors retain old filenames or frontmatter.
preMortem.consequence: Codex/Claude users still see or invoke koala-* roles, and verify_codex fails or misses drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Rename template files and mirrored assets together, update manifest/managed-asset expectations, then run node bin/lattice.js verify_codex.

preMortem.scenario: Execution document overclaims that every Koala token is gone.
preMortem.trigger: Runtime compatibility paths like KOALA_* env vars or .koala legacy archive references are still intentionally present.
preMortem.consequence: Future hosts treat intentional compatibility material as unfinished cleanup or accidentally delete needed migration support.
preMortem.mitigation: Document the active-role boundary clearly and include rg verification patterns that separate role IDs from legacy runtime compatibility tokens.

preMortem.scenario: Tests fail due to stale expected strings and salts.
preMortem.trigger: Smoke tasks and process fact contract scripts still assert koala-review-* names or koala integrity salt strings.
preMortem.mitigation: Update tests and scripts alongside runtime code, keeping signature salt changes deliberate and documented in the execution plan.
